statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-41567 (GHSA-x86f-5xw2-fm2r, GO-2026-5746): in the Docker Engine daemon before 29.5.1 (github.com/docker/docker 28.5.2 and earlier, moby/moby v2 before 2.0.0-beta.14), uploading a compressed archive to a container through PUT /containers/{id}/archive or docker cp - makes the daemon run the decompression program (xz or unpigz) from the container's filesystem, so a malicious image can run code with the daemon's privileges. It is fixed in Docker Engine 29.5.1: https://github.com/moby/moby/security/advisories/GHSA-x86f-5xw2-fm2r. This package contains no Go program. We unpacked every published docker-dind-dev package for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI Alpine repository, 29.7.2-r0 to 29.10.0-r3 (59 builds, each for x86_64 and aarch64), after verifying each against its index checksum: the payload of each is the three shell scripts docker-entrypoint.sh, dockerd-entrypoint.sh and modprobe (29.7.2-r1 ships modprobe as /usr/lib/docker-dind/modprobe.sh), plus, from 29.9.2-r9 on, an SPDX document, opt/docker/sbom/docker-dind-runtime/.spdx.docker-dind-runtime.json, describing the programs of the separate packages it depends on. That document lists github.com/docker/docker 28.5.2 as a module of those programs, but it is a JSON text file, not code. No build contains an ELF, PE or Mach-O file, a static archive or any other compiled program. github.com/docker/docker reaches an image only inside those separately packaged programs, such as the Docker Engine, containerd and Buildx packages, which are assessed as their own owners.

CVE-2026-41567 (GO-2026-5746, GHSA-x86f-5xw2-fm2r): when the Docker daemon handles PUT /containers/{id}/archive with a compressed archive, it runs the decompression binary from the container's filesystem with the daemon's privileges. The Go vulnerability database names Daemon.containerExtractToDir in the daemon package of github.com/docker/docker, github.com/moby/moby and github.com/moby/moby/v2 as the vulnerable function; only github.com/moby/moby/v2 has a fixed Go release (2.0.0-beta.14), and the Docker Engine 29.5.1 fix changes daemon/archive_unix.go and an integration test: https://github.com/moby/moby/security/advisories/GHSA-x86f-5xw2-fm2r, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5746, https://github.com/moby/moby/commit/2022313ffe5a8c04890b5295bc52670ee6df8070. Read every published trivy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 38 builds, 0.69.1-r0 to the current 0.74.0-r12, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against the checksum in the package index. Each package installs one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 that keeps its symbol table. The Go build information of /usr/bin/trivy lists github.com/docker/docker v28.5.2+incompatible in 0.69.1-r0 to 0.69.3-r7 and does not list it from 0.70.0-r0; every build lists the separate github.com/moby/moby/api and github.com/moby/moby/client modules, and none lists github.com/moby/moby or github.com/moby/moby/v2. In the builds that list it, the github.com/docker/docker packages with functions in the binary's symbol table are the Docker API client (client) and API types (api/types and its network, strslice, swarm/runtime and versions subpackages). No binary in any build has a function from the daemon package of github.com/docker/docker, github.com/moby/moby or github.com/moby/moby/v2 in its symbol table (read with go tool nm, which lists runtime.main in every binary), and no binary contains those package paths or the name containerExtractToDir as raw bytes, so the vulnerable daemon code is not present. As a positive control, the same patterns find github.com/moby/moby/v2/daemon.(*Daemon).containerExtractToDir in the function table, and the daemon package path and the name containerExtractToDir in the bytes, of /usr/bin/dockerd in the DHI docker-engine 29.10.0-r1 package for Alpine 3.23 on x86_64 and aarch64.

CVE-2026-41567 (GHSA-x86f-5xw2-fm2r, GO-2026-5746): the Docker daemon's PUT /containers/{id}/archive handler can execute a binary from the container on the host; the vulnerable code is Daemon.containerExtractToDir in the github.com/docker/docker/daemon package (https://github.com/moby/moby/security/advisories/GHSA-x86f-5xw2-fm2r, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5746). Read every published alloy-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository, 1.18.1-0 to 1.22.0-16, on amd64 and arm64 (1.21.2-0 was published for arm64 only); 87 packages, with no debug-symbol packages published for this source. By build, the Go build information of /usr/bin/alloy lists github.com/docker/docker as 1.18.1-0 to 1.19.2-7: 28.5.2+incompatible; 1.20.1-0 to 1.22.0-16: not listed; where it is listed, Alloy uses it as a client library for the Docker API. In no build does /usr/bin/alloy contain any function from the Docker daemon (github.com/docker/docker/daemon), checked against the function names the Go linker records in each binary, so the vulnerable daemon code is not compiled in. The same check finds Daemon.containerExtractToDir in the dockerd program of the DHI docker-ce 5:29.6.2-2 package, which shows that it detects the daemon code where it is compiled in.
